# Temp Plots

```{r}
#import temp file
mat_df <- readMat.default(con = "data/metadata/LSEO24h_temp.mat")

# Extract dataframe we want from 'T' for temp and convert matlab time to poxit time
temp_df <- mat_df$T |> 
  as.data.frame()
# Set colnames and rownames
colnames(temp_df) <- mat_df$dep  
rownames(temp_df) <- mat_df$t 
# move dttm column out, convert to datetime and pivot long
temp_df_long <- temp_df |> 
  rownames_to_column(var = "dttm") |>
  mutate(dttm = as_datetime((as.numeric(dttm) - 719529) * 86400)) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = !dttm, names_to = "depth", values_to = "temp") |> 
# Add averaged temperature column
  mutate(date = round_date(dttm, unit = "day"), 
  depth = as.numeric(depth)) |> 
  group_by(date, depth) |> 
  mutate(temp_c_24h_avg = mean(temp)) |> 
  ungroup()

## Create a 14 day averaged temperature---------------------------------
locs <- seaprocess::find_near(vec = as_date(temp_df_long$date), vals = as_date(sw_meta$date))
dates <- as_date(rep(NA, nrow(temp_df_long)))
for(i in length(locs):1) {
dates[1:locs[i]] <- as_date(sw_meta$date[i])
}
rm(i)
# Add the 14ish day average
temp_df_long<-temp_df_long |>
  mutate(sample_date = dates) |> 
  group_by(sample_date, depth) |> 
  mutate(temp_c_14d_avg = mean(temp)) |> 
  ungroup()

temp_plot <- temp_df_long |> 
  mutate(depth = as.numeric(depth), color = depth) |> 
  filter(depth < 50) |> 
  ggplot(aes(dttm, temp_c_24h_avg)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = sw_meta$date) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = sw_meta$date[which(sw_meta$sample == sw_meta$sample[6:10])], color = "red") +
    geom_point() +
    scale_color_grey() +
    geom_point(data = temp_df_long[temp_df_long$depth == 38,], color = "red") +
    theme(legend.position = "none") + 
    theme_classic()

temp_plot


```

# Interpretation

See a big drop in diversity at WM19 in both 16s and sylph, both are less consistent in the initial months. WM19 is at the end of April beginning of May when the water column is weakly stratified.

Compositional Samples: Samples that describe the relative composition of organisms in a sample. This ignore the total number of organisms counted. For example in WM01 we might have gotten 100 reads back that mapped to A B C and D equally. However in WM02 we only got a 10 reads back that mapped to A B C and D equally. These samples are counted as equals. However if we were out taking net samples. A sample with only 10 individuals would be different than our sample with 100 individuals. Because we cannot standardize the number of reads very well we think of microbial samples as compositional -- we care about their composition rather than absolute abundances. IE everything is already normalized to 0 to 1..

Also looked at a couple other books like Tuomas Borman, Leo Lahti, Sudarshan Shetty, Felix M Ernst, et al. 2026. Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis with Bioconductor \[Beta Version\]. microbiome.github.io/oma/. on github.

# June 24, 2026

Writeup of how I filtered contamination:

From 16S taxa:

1\) Filtered out any taxa associated with the Synthetic Mock community

2\) Ran micRoclean package with associated well numbers (found from initial sample submission sheet). I used their "pipeline 1" to search for the original composition of the samples. I treated samples WM17-WM24 (s_2425) as blanks because they did not pump. This was the most conservative option.

3\) Narrowed down taxa to just those that remained abundant in the samples

4\) Look through each of the taxa from "Sheik et al, 2018." For each taxa I looked to see if it could reasonably be found in pelagic Lake Superior. This consisted of a quick google search. I kept taxa were found in freshwater. Reasoning can be found in ("02.1_import_clean_16s_data.R").

For MAGs:

1\) I worked under the assumption that if we had a taxa in the MAGs then it would also be in the 16S dataset.

2\) I imported all 800 bins from all samples

3\) removed all the bins from WM17-WM24

4\) Removed the bins that matched the family and genus of a possible contaminant taxa from the 16S dataset. In this I also had a fuzzy match for names that differed slightly. I combed through those by hand and removed matches

5\) Afterwards was left with \~300 bins for CoverM and dereplication

6\) I filtered just to keep the bins that had abunance calculated. 

Also starting working through the microtrait results. I should continue to look at these tomorrow. For now, I have two good microtables and some data to move forward with.
